claim.pdf_says: In the PICTURE Format 1 diagram the word FOR is printed UNDERLINED (verified by rendering page 471 at 300 dpi and cropping the FOR group: 'FOR' carries a rule beneath it, exactly as NEGATIVE and POSITIVE do).
claim.markdown_says: First figure-notes paragraph: '**Figure notes (PICTURE clause Format 1 (basic) syntax diagram).** `PICTURE`, `PIC`, `EDITING`, `NEGATIVE`, and `POSITIVE` are underlined in the printed standard (required words / required minimum abbreviation).' — `FOR` is omitted from the list of underlined words. (The second, duplicate note on the same page does list `FOR` as underlined, so the two notes contradict each other.)
claim.why_it_matters: Per 5.2.6, an underlined word in a general format is a REQUIRED word that shall be written when the phrase is used; a non-underlined word is an optional word that may be omitted. Omitting FOR from the underlined list makes the FOR keyword look omissible, i.e. it would legalise 'EDITING c NEGATIVE IS lit-2' with no FOR — a grammar the standard does not permit. This is the falsely-permissive mirror of the usual defect and it is directly load-bearing for the PICTURE EDITING parser.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED on both sides, with independent pixel measurement rather than visual impression.

PDF SIDE — FOR is unambiguously underlined. Rendered page 471 at 300 dpi (E:/Temp/specrecon/v471/spec_p471.png, 2550x3300) and ran a per-row ink profile over each word's bounding box, counting pixels < 128 luma and flagging any row >= 70% filled (an underline rule) that sits below the glyph band:
  - FOR (x 1546-1622, window 76 px): glyph rows 1162-1191; then a clean 13-row white gap; then a solid 2-row rule at y = 1205-1206 measuring 70 and 72 of 76 px (92-95% fill). That is a rule, not glyph ink.
  - NEGATIVE (x 1702-1906, window 204 px): glyphs 1128-1157; rule at y = 1172-1173, 195/204 px.
  - POSITIVE (same x): glyphs 1200-1229; rule at y = 1244-1245, 176/204 px.
  - IS literal-2 (x 1920-2120, window 200 px) — the control: glyphs 1127-1157 and NO row anywhere near the rule threshold. Correctly not underlined.
FOR therefore carries the same underline signature (same 2-px stroke weight, same ~14-px baseline offset, same >90% span of the word width) as the two words the markdown already concedes are underlined, and is structurally distinct from the non-underlined IS/literal control. The visual crop (E:/Temp/specrecon/v471/crop_for.png, 3x LANCZOS) shows the same thing plainly.

MARKDOWN SIDE — the quote is exact and the omission is real. specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 19956-19957 read: '**Figure notes (PICTURE clause Format 1 (basic) syntax diagram).** `PICTURE`, `PIC`, `EDITING`, `NEGATIVE`, and / `POSITIVE` are underlined in the printed standard (required words / required minimum abbreviation).' FOR is absent. This is not a line-wrap or reflow artifact: I read both physical lines of the wrapped sentence and the enumeration closes with 'and `POSITIVE`'. Line 19970, the duplicate note, reads '`PICTURE`, `PIC`, `EDITING`, `FOR`, `NEGATIVE`, and `POSITIVE` are underlined ...; `IS`, `character-string-1`, `character-1`, and the literals are not.' The two notes for the same figure genuinely contradict each other.

WHY THIS CHANGES MEANING (i.e. why it is not mere formatting). The ASCII/box-drawing diagram blocks in this transcription carry no underline information at all — the figure note is the SOLE channel by which the keyword/optional-word distinction survives transcription. Across the transcription these notes are written as exhaustive enumerations, frequently with an explicit negative half (e.g. line 4315: '`ALL` and `ON` are **not** underlined'). A reader or extractor consuming the first note therefore concludes FOR is an optional word.

I tested the strongest available refutations and all fail: the word is not present on an adjacent line; this is not page-break furniture, wrapping or hyphenation; neither source is misquoted; and the difference is squarely semantic, not cosmetic.

One partial mitigation, recorded for honesty rather than as a refutation: the first note omits FOR but does not affirmatively assert that FOR is un-underlined — it lacks the '...are not' clause the second note has. So it is a misleading omission from an exhaustive-looking list rather than an explicit false statement. Given that the note is the only carrier of underlining, the practical effect is the one the claim describes.
verdict.corrected_description:
REAL, with two corrections to the claim as filed.

(1) CITATION CORRECTION. The claim cites 5.2.6 for the underline convention. 5.2.6 is 'Options' and governs brackets, braces and choice indicators only. The underline convention is 5.2.2 Keywords ('Keywords are reserved words or context-sensitive words. They are shown in uppercase and underlined in general formats. They are required in order to select the functionality associated with that keyword...' — specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 2628) and 5.2.3 Optional words ('...shown in uppercase and not underlined in general formats. They may be written to add clarity...' — line 2641). The claim's substantive reasoning is right; only the section number is wrong. Cite 5.2.2/5.2.3, not 5.2.6.

(2) THE ROOT DEFECT IS LARGER THAN THE UNDERLINE LIST, and fixing it fixes this. The PDF prints the Format 1 (basic) diagram EXACTLY ONCE, immediately followed by 'Format 2 (locale):'. The markdown contains the Format 1 diagram plus its figure note TWICE: block A at lines 19950-19962 and block B at lines 19964-19971. Block A is the stale/inferior copy — it is the one missing FOR from the underlined list, and its inner stack is also more crudely rendered ('⎧|' / '⎩|' for the inner braces versus block B's better-formed '⎨ |'). Block B is complete and correct: it lists FOR as underlined and adds the negative half naming IS, character-string-1, character-1 and the literals as not underlined. Both blocks otherwise agree that the FOR group is enclosed in choice indicators (correct — the bars are visible in the render at x ~1660 and ~1990, and per 5.2.6.4 braces around choice indicators mean one or more of NEGATIVE/POSITIVE, each at most once, in any order).

RECOMMENDED FIX: delete duplicate block A (lines 19950-19962) in its entirety and keep block B. That simultaneously removes the spurious second diagram the PDF does not print and eliminates the contradictory, FOR-omitting figure note — a single deletion resolving both defects. Do not 'fix' block A by adding FOR to its list, which would leave the spurious duplicate diagram in place.

NORMATIVE IMPACT AS FILED IS UPHELD: FOR is a keyword and shall be written whenever the NEGATIVE/POSITIVE choice-indicator group is specified. 'EDITING character-1 NEGATIVE IS literal-2' without FOR is not legal COBOL, and the PICTURE EDITING parser must require the FOR keyword before the NEGATIVE/POSITIVE group.
